messages.displayText:
Research assistants wanted! Carry out
simple tasks, such as catching Pokémon,
to earn extravagant rewards!

Help keep Lumiose clean by picking up
any items or litter you find on the streets.

This symbol of the city gazes down
on all of Lumiose and has long been
beloved by its people.

Lumiose City is dotted with artworks,
statues, and fountains depicting the
Pokémon our citizens love and respect.

From our scaffolding projects to urban
redevelopment and even home remodels—
Racine is here to fill the city with smiles!

Kalos’s greatest actress, Diantha,
is back in a new film—coming soon
to theaters near you!

Discover the lives of the people who first
came to live alongside Pokémon in this
traveling exhibit at the Lumiose Museum!

Try the delicious taste sensation that’s
spread across the world! We deliver the
freshest catches from Azure Bay to you.

Have your Pokémon use their moves to
smash clusters of Mega Crystals and help
remove these eyesores from our fair city!

The Lumiose City Gym is currently
closed due to renovation work on
Prism Tower.

To those interested in a beautiful lifestyle
alongside Pokémon, the Lumiose Society
of Battle Connoisseurs welcomes you.

Each café in Lumiose City is proud to
present its own unique menu of drinks.
Please enjoy them with your Pokémon!

We’re hard at work redeveloping
Lumiose City to serve our increasing
population of wild Pokémon neighbors.

A one-star restaurant where you can
relax and enjoy the cuisine of Kalos in
a casual atmosphere.

A two-star restaurant known widely
for its aspiration to offer a first-class
dining experience.

A prestigious three-star restaurant that is
renowned for its multicourse meals and
hailed as being very much worth a visit.

This restaurant, which operates in other
regions as well, is officially named the
Sushi High Roller Bistro.

Pokémon raised by people seem to grow
stronger than those that live in the wild.

Even Pokémon of the same species
will demonstrate some differences in
strength from one individual to another.

Taking another Trainer’s Pokémon makes
you a thief. Only throw Poké Balls at wild
Pokémon that you want to catch!

When you want to be sure a move will
land or a Poké Ball will hit your target,
remember to use <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0002>ZL to focus on it!

Wild Pokémon wander our city, even
outside of wild zones. If one comes at
you with an attack, use <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0004>Sp_2 to dodge!

If you want to change your outfit, use
<U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0004>Sp_1 to open the main menu, then press
<U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0005>Minus to give yourself a fresh look.

Don’t throw away your future—throw
Poké Balls instead! To throw a Poké Ball
at a target, use <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0002>ZR!

If you hit a wild Pokémon with a move
and it becomes dazed, that’s your catch
window! Throw a Poké Ball!

Press <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0004>Plus to open your map. From there,
you’ll be able to select a spot to travel
to and zip right over in an instant!

If you want to dash, press <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0006>Cancel!
You’ll keep up a brisk pace as
long as you don’t stop moving.

Not all Pokémon evolve by leveling
up—some need to have specific items
used on them in order to evolve.

Pokémon with a high Speed stat
won’t have to wait as long between
using their moves in battle.

Pokémon can learn moves by
leveling up or by using TMs—
short for Technical Machines!

When a Pokémon uses one of its
moves as a Plus Move, it won’t need
to wait as long as usual to use it!

While focused on a target, you can
move <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+0007>Stick_R up, down, left, or right to
switch focus to another nearby target.

Pokémon Centers, cafés, and the like
will be registered as travel spots after
you visit them for the first time.

Some moves can be affected by weather.
For example, rain weakens Fire-type moves
but gives Water-type moves a small boost.

Lumiose is simply bursting with cafés!
And word has it that Pokémon enjoy
relaxing in cafés as much as people do.

When you feel there’s no hope of winning
in a Z-A Royale battle, choose to forfeit.
You can always earn more medals later.

Any Pokémon you obtain by trading with
another Trainer will get a small boost to
the Exp. Points it receives as it grows.

If you’re in the market for Mega Stones,
consider a visit to the Stone Emporium
or Quasartico Inc. for all your needs!

If you use <U+0010><U+0002>봊<U+000C>Stick_L_Push to crouch, you can hide in
patches of tall grass or behind objects.
Pokémon will be less likely to spot you!

Your Pokémon will grow more friendly
toward you if you spend time relaxing
at cafés together.

Have your Pokémon unleash as many
moves as possible—it will cause that
Pokémon to build up Mega Power!

Some Pokémon only evolve during
certain times of the day.

A Pokémon whose Trainer is nearby will
gain more Mega Power using moves than
a Pokémon whose Trainer is far away!

Supereffective moves deal even more
damage if they are used as Plus Moves!

When moves are used as Plus Moves,
their power is boosted and their area
of effect becomes larger than usual.

Visit the front desk at Quasartico Inc. to
trade your Mega Shards for other items!

Stop by Racine Construction to trade
your Colorful Screws for other items!

When battling against a wild Pokémon,
you’ll find you can’t do certain things—
such as moving to travel spots.

If you don’t send out your own Pokémon
when facing wild Pokémon, any incoming
attacks will be directed at you instead!

Want to evolve a Pokémon? You can do
that while viewing your current party!

Want to give your Pokémon nicknames?
You can do that right from your Boxes!

Pokémon with a high Speed stat won’t
have to wait as long to unleash their
moves in battle.

If you pick up any Tiny Mushrooms or
Pretty Feathers, feel free to sell them
at your local Pokémon Center!

If your Pokémon is poisoned, it will
keep on losing HP! Be sure to heal it
up as soon as you can.

Even moves like Protect or Detect don’t
stand a chance of blocking Plus Moves!

The heavier a Pokémon is, the harder it
might be to knock it back with a move.

New moves your Pokémon learn appear in
their Available Moves list. You can change
current moves from your team or Boxes.

Pokémon received from other Trainers
in trades gain Exp. Points at a slightly
higher rate, making them easier to raise.

This isn’t really a tip at all, but have you
counted how many Trainer Tips boards
Lumiose City has in total?

Making good use of Roto-Glide when
navigating scaffolding may help you find
your way up to some tricky spots.

Buy 10 Poké Balls of the same variety
in a single purchase to receive one
Premier Ball on the house!

Word on the street is that there are
some places in Lumiose you can only
reach via the rooftops.

Rumor has it that the more Canari plush
you collect, the more mysterious benefits
you’ll reap from them!

People say that alpha Pokémon have
been making their homes on the
rooftops of our fair city.

You’ll often find Flying-type Pokémon
on the roofs of buildings.

Large outbreaks of Mega Crystals
can be found growing on rooftops
at times. Keep an eye out for them!

You can’t jump to any travel spots
when you’re belowground.

There are some species of Pokémon that
never show themselves during the day.
Try searching for them at different times!

There are many twists and turns here,
meaning plenty of blind corners. Take
care not to give away your location.

The water may restrict your ability to move
about. Take care not to become an easy
target if you cross the small bridge!

Be wary of any objects around this simple
landscape if you don’t want to be caught
unawares—they may conceal opponents.

The sewers create a difference in elevation
within this zone. Keep that in mind when
strategizing and navigating the terrain.

You can get a clear line of sight along
Estival Avenue in this zone. Using that to
your advantage will be your key to victory.

If you wish to reach the rooftops, you’ll
need to tackle some tricky scaffolding
in this tough-to-navigate battle zone.

The mazelike streets in this zone require
special care to navigate if you hope to
remain unnoticed by opponents.

The long, narrow streets here make it a
good idea to take advantage of objects
that can shield you from being spotted.

Buildings loom over most areas in this
zone. The streets are also wide open,
making them hard to traverse undetected.

There are lots of wide-open spaces in this
sprawling zone, making you an easy target
for other Trainers taking part in the Royale.

The stairs and little paths you might not
even notice during daytime hours require
strategic approaches in this battle zone.

Be ready for attacks from wild Pokémon if
you’re going to enter this wild zone!

Keep an eye out for Pokémon when using
the bridges or approaching the water here.

The fences here make it hard to run freely.
Don’t forget to explore the building!

This graveyard contains lots of hiding
places, so use stealth to your advantage.

This zone is spacious but has few hiding
spots, even in the sewers. Move with care!

This zone offers multiple heights to
explore, from rooftops down to the canal.

The tall grass is your ally in this wide-open
plaza. The central obelisk is worth a look.

Many Ground-type Pokémon live here.
Watch out for the mounds of dirt!

The scaffolding makes this zone tricky.
Don’t forget to explore the rooftops!

Explore both rooftops and waterways here.
Pokémon may leap from the water!

The Saison Canal divides this zone in two.
Accessing the other side may be tricky.

There is a distinct chill permeating this
zone. Be careful to avoid getting frozen!

The Bug-type Pokémon in this zone will
attack interlopers relentlessly.

Use the substation’s buildings and
equipment to sneak as best you can.

This narrow zone gives little room to hide.
Pokémon vary greatly from day to night.

Watch out for obstacles when throwing
Poké Balls in this zone of varied terrain.

There’s little to hide behind. You may well
get surrounded by wild Pokémon here.

Use the alleyway and scaffolding wisely to
navigate around the tall buildings here.

Try to hide yourself behind the greenery
to sneak up on wild Pokémon undetected.

The highest-level wild zone in all of
Lumiose City!

Trainer tip message

Donuts with Sparkling Power will make it
easier for you to find Shiny Pokémon
during visits to Hyperspace Lumiose.

The higher your donut’s Flavor Score, the
greater the Level Boost it’ll give your
Pokémon in Hyperspace Lumiose.

If you complete three hyperspace tasks in
a visit to Hyperspace Lumiose, a golden
Poké Ball full of items will appear!
